tuition.notes: The official bachelor's pages say citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA/Scandinavia must pay tuition fees (unless a residence permit exempts them) but give NO bachelor's fee amount. The figures that do appear on official pages (EUR 10,000 to 17,000 per academic year, and DKK 75,000 on one programme page) apply to master's programmes only. Application fee for non-EU applicants: DKK 1,120 (stated for master's applications).

language_tests: Danish at the highest level (Danish A, or 'Studieprøven i dansk som andetsprog'): all bachelor's programmes are taught in Danish
required_documents: Non-EU citizens: documentation of residence permit
requirements.other: Programme-specific subject levels equivalent to the Danish levels A (advanced), B (intermediate) and C (elementary). EU/EEA diplomas: a grade point average equivalent to the Danish 6.0 or more is needed to apply through quota 1 (Danish scale, not 4.0). IB/EB holders can apply through quota 1 and quota 2. English test minimums for bachelor's are not stated.

bachelor.financial_aid_summary: No scholarships for bachelor's students are listed on the official pages reviewed. The official fee-waiver pages describe waivers for non-EU master's applicants only.
key_deadlines: Application deadline: 15 March at 12:00 (applicants with international degrees)
Supplementary documents for admission requirements: no later than 5 July at 12:00
bachelor.notes: IMPORTANT: the University of Copenhagen only offers bachelor's programmes taught in Danish (78 programmes), so an international applicant needs Danish at the highest level. Third-party sites that quote non-EU 'tuition ranges' are describing master's programmes. The programme list below is only a sample of the 78 programmes.

tuition.international: Set per course. One 2027/28 non-EU year-1 example: EUR 26,220 (Intellectual Disability Nursing). Check the official fee schedule for your course.
tuition.notes: Official wording: 'The Tuition fees noted in the below fee schedule relates to the first year of the course, not the fee for entire course duration.' Fees rise each year for continuing students (2.33% a year for the 2026/27 intake, 3% a year for the 2027/28 intake). Fee status depends on residence, not nationality; EU students pay the Student Contribution Fee. Non-EU undergraduates pay a deposit on accepting an offer, and everyone pays an annual 'Student Levies and Charges' fee. The full 2027/28 course-by-course schedule was not captured.

language_tests: IELTS: 6.5 overall (6 in each band)
TOEFL iBT: 90 (21 in each section)
Duolingo English Test: 120/160 (100 in each subscore)
PTE Academic: 69 (59 in each section)
Cambridge C1 Advanced / C2 Proficiency: 180 (no score below 170)
standardized_tests: SAT or ACT (optional for US applicants; typical ranges SAT 1250 to 1400, ACT 27 to 32)
Extra assessments for some courses (for example Music, Drama)
requirements.other: Six subjects, including passes in English and Mathematics and usually a language other than English. Typical academic ranges in the international admissions guide: A-Levels A*A*A to ABB depending on the course; IB 30 to 40 points; US unweighted GPA 3.2 to 3.5 out of 4.0; China Gaokao Band 3 (GK 68%, HS 80%); India Standard XII 75 to 90. Programme subject requirements and competitive bands also apply. Some programmes need higher English scores (for example Dental, Clinical Speech and Language Studies). Non-EU applicants apply directly to Trinity (my.tcd.ie), not through the CAO.

scholarships.name: Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: Students with non-EU fee status holding a 2026/27 offer; excludes Medicine, Dentistry, Acting, Engineering, Natural Sciences and Computer Science & Statistics. The 2027/28 version is not stated.
scholarships.amount: EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000 depending on the region (year-1 fee reduction only)

scholarships.name: Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.amount: Non-EU scholars have their fees reduced to the EU fee-paying level

bachelor.financial_aid_summary: The Global Excellence scholarship reduces first-year fees only and excludes the programmes with the highest fees. The Foundation Scholarship (by examination, after enrolment) reduces fees for non-EU scholars to the EU fee-paying level.
bachelor.notes: Four-year degrees. Deadlines for 2027 non-EU direct entry are not stated on the pages reviewed. The programme list below is a sample of the roughly 70 programmes and joint-honours subjects in the admissions guide.
fields_of_study: Philosophy, Political Science, Economics and Sociology

tuition.domestic_or_home: No tuition fee is stated for undergraduates (a semester contribution applies)
tuition.international: No tuition fee is stated for undergraduates (a semester contribution applies)
tuition.notes: The bachelor's semester contribution is not stated on the central pages reviewed. Department pages mention around EUR 350 to 355 per semester, including a public transport ticket (LL.M. and master's pages).

language_tests: German C1 certificate required to apply (Goethe-Zertifikat C1, telc C1, telc C1 Hochschule or DSH-1), then the DSH must be taken before enrolment
TestDaF with at least level 4 in all sections exempts from the DSH
standardized_tests: DSH (German language entrance exam) before enrolment, unless exempt
required_documents: Recognised school-leaving qualification, assessed via uni-assist for foreign certificates
requirements.other: All undergraduate degree programmes are offered exclusively in German. Many programmes have a numerus clausus. Minimum grades and tests are not stated on the pages reviewed. HU does not organise preparatory German courses.

bachelor.financial_aid_summary: Scholarships are not stated on the official pages reviewed.
key_deadlines: 15 July for the following winter term (stated on the Library and Information Science BA page); international applicants apply via uni-assist
bachelor.notes: IMPORTANT: there is no English-taught bachelor's at Humboldt; English-taught options exist only at master's level. Being tuition-free does not make it accessible: certified C1 German is needed just to apply. The programme list and count were not captured.

tuition.domestic_or_home: No tuition fees for citizens of the EU, EEA and Switzerland
tuition.international: Quoted as a total for the whole programme, not per year. Examples: International Business SEK 390,000 in total (first payment SEK 65,000); Development Studies SEK 375,000; Music (Individual Programme) SEK 585,000; Fine Arts SEK 615,000.
tuition.notes: Programme pages show the full programme fee, not an annual fee. Application fee: SEK 900 per semester round.

language_tests: English 6 / English level 2 (Swedish upper-secondary level); IELTS and TOEFL equivalences are not stated on the pages reviewed
requirements.other: Example, International Business: general entry requirements plus Mathematics 3b/3c and Social Studies 1b. In the early international admissions round seats are allocated entirely by the general average (GPA) of your higher secondary school leaving certificate. Applications go through universityadmissions.se. Lund also has many bachelor's programmes taught in Swedish.

scholarships.name: Lund University Global Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Merit-based, for non-EU/EEA applicants; primarily for master's applicants. Bachelor's programmes eligible: Development Studies, Mathematics, Physics and Physical Geography (International Business is not eligible).

bachelor.financial_aid_summary: The Lund University Global Scholarship is mainly for master's applicants; the only bachelor's programmes it covers are Development Studies, Mathematics, Physics and Physical Geography. Amounts and deadlines are not stated on the pages reviewed.
bachelor.notes: Ten bachelor's programmes are taught in English (Lund's official Facts and figures page); the other bachelor's programmes are taught in Swedish.
fields_of_study: Music - Performance Programme in Folk and World Music

tuition.domestic_or_home: No tuition fee for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens and holders of Finnish permanent residence
tuition.international: EUR 13,000 per academic year for the English-language bachelor's programmes (non-EU/EEA applicants)
tuition.notes: National application fee: EUR 100 for non-EU applicants. Student Union fee: EUR 85 for 2026-27.

standardized_tests: SAT or ACT: required for Admission group 1 (admission is based on the scores)
requirements.other: Admission group 1 (no IB, EB or Finnish matriculation qualification): admission is based on SAT or ACT scores. Admission group 2 (IB, EB, Finnish matriculation exam, or Reifeprüfung/DIA in Finland): certificate-based. You cannot choose your group; your previous education decides it. English test minimums are not stated on the pages captured (see Helsinki's 'Proving your English language skills' page). Full criteria are on Studyinfo.fi.

scholarships.name: Master's tuition-fee waiver for Science BSc graduates
scholarships.eligibility: Graduates of the Science BSc who finish on time with a minimum GPA of 3.8 out of 5
scholarships.amount: 100% tuition waiver for a Helsinki master's programme

bachelor.financial_aid_summary: There are no tuition fee waivers for applicants to the English-language bachelor's degrees.

Autumn 2027, Admission group 2: 9 to 23 March 2027 (closes 15:00 Finnish time)
bachelor.notes: Only two bachelor's programmes are taught in English (Liberal Arts and Sciences, and Science); all other bachelor's programmes are in Finnish and/or Swedish. In the Science BSc at least 75% of the credits, including the thesis, must be completed in English. Group 1 applicants need SAT/ACT results before January.

tuition.notes: Graduation fee: EUR 215. Partial exemptions of 100% to 20% are available depending on family economic condition. The World Bachelor in Business is priced separately (2025-26: Year 3 at Bocconi EUR 25,000). Several official fee pages are flagged 'Being updated'.

standardized_tests: Engineering: TOL (Italian), TOLC-I, CEnT-S (English) or SAT (2026/27 early enrolment: at least 620 in each SAT section; 2027/28 Italian-taught early phase: SAT converted to at least 75/100)

New English-taught engineering bachelor's programmes (Engineering Science, Industrial Engineering, Process Engineering) were pending ministerial approval.
